depends_on: Dusart 2010 Prop. 6.8: prime in (x, x(1+1/(25 ln^2 x))] for x >= 396738
notes: True: 2^n is a sum of n distinct primes for n >= 6. Richert-style induction on the number k of odd primes: if every N' = k mod 2 in [L_k, B_k] is a sum of k distinct odd primes, then every N = k+1 mod 2 in [2L_k/(1-1/(25 ln^2 L_k)), 2B_k] is, taking a prime p in (N/2, (N/2)(1+eps)] (Dusart) above all primes of N-p. Base k=22 on [0.9*2^22, 2^23] by computer; L_k/2^k stays below 0.95 and B_k = 2^(k+1), covering 2^n (n even) and 2^n - 2 (n odd, plus prime 2). Explicit representations for 6 <= n <= 23. Outside Lean: everything (Dusart's theorem, base computation).

sources.cite: P. Dusart, Estimates of some functions over primes without R.H., arXiv:1002.0442 (2010), Prop. 6.8
